rituals.name: TWO TRUTHS, TWO HANDS
rituals.title: TWO TRUTHS, TWO HANDS
rituals.targetPattern: Belief conflicting feelings mean indecision or hypocrisy
rituals.target_pattern: Belief conflicting feelings mean indecision or hypocrisy
rituals.precise_subpattern: Belief conflicting feelings mean indecision or hypocrisy
rituals.vibeLine: Nobody has to win this round.
rituals.hook: Give each side a hand so neither has to shout over the other.
rituals.predict: Guess which hand feels heavier: “I want this” or “I’m scared of this.”
rituals.play: Hold one palm up for the want and the other for the fear. Say one honest sentence to each hand. Don’t force a winner.
rituals.catch: Check if the conflict feels different when both truths are allowed to exist at once.
rituals.reveal: Ambivalence is not necessarily confusion; sometimes it is two valid systems reporting simultaneously.
rituals.mindBend: Wanting something and fearing it can both be true without cancelling each other.

Give each side a hand so neither has to shout over the other.
cheeky.ritualCard:
Give each side a hand so neither has to shout over the other.
Hold one palm up for the want and the other for the fear. Say one honest sentence to each hand. Don’t force a winner.
Guess which hand feels heavier: “I want this” or “I’m scared of this.”
Check if the conflict feels different when both truths are allowed to exist at once. Ambivalence is not necessarily confusion; sometimes it is two valid systems reporting simultaneously.

rituals.name: ALARM / STORY SPLIT
rituals.title: ALARM / STORY SPLIT
rituals.targetPattern: Body alarm fused with catastrophic explanation
rituals.target_pattern: Body alarm fused with catastrophic explanation
rituals.precise_subpattern: Body alarm fused with catastrophic explanation
rituals.vibeLine: Your body rang the alarm. Your mind immediately wrote the press release.
rituals.hook: Separate the siren from the news report.
rituals.predict: Guess which part arrives first: body alarm or explanatory story.
rituals.play: Say two lines only: “Alarm: ____” using body sensations. “Story: ____” using the meaning your mind adds. Keep them on separate lines.
rituals.catch: Check if the story still feels identical to the alarm once they are visually separated.
rituals.reveal: A nervous system signal and an explanation can arrive together without being the same evidence.
rituals.mindBend: The alarm can be real even when the story about the alarm is wrong.

rituals.title: URGE HAND / VALUE HAND
rituals.targetPattern: Urge and value treated as mutually exclusive
rituals.target_pattern: Urge and value treated as mutually exclusive
rituals.precise_subpattern: Urge and value treated as mutually exclusive
rituals.vibeLine: Urge can complain from the passenger seat.
rituals.hook: Let the urge exist without making it the steering wheel.
rituals.predict: Guess which hand moves first when you imagine the next thirty seconds.
rituals.play: Put one hand forward for the immediate urge and one for the longer-term value. Move both hands slightly in the direction each wants. Choose one centimetre of movement for the value hand without hiding the urge hand.
rituals.catch: Notice that action can align with one system while the other system is still present.
rituals.reveal: You do not need an urge to disappear before acting beside it.
rituals.mindBend: Alignment is choosing a direction while competing signals are still talking.

rituals.targetPattern: Dislike confused with probability
rituals.target_pattern: Dislike confused with probability
rituals.precise_subpattern: Dislike confused with probability
rituals.vibeLine: Hating an outcome does not make your forecast department smarter.
rituals.hook: Your brain may be answering “Will it happen?”
rituals.predict: Guess which sentence is actually stronger in you: the forecast or the preference.
rituals.play: Say both separately: “I predict ____ will happen.” Then: “I really Don’t want ____ to happen.” Rate each sentence from 0–10 for certainty/intensity.
rituals.catch: Check if emotional intensity is being used as if it were probability evidence.
rituals.reveal: Strong preference against an outcome can make the outcome feel more likely without adding predictive information.
rituals.mindBend: Not wanting something is not evidence that it is coming.

rituals.title: BODY BEFORE BIOGRAPHY
rituals.targetPattern: Explaining body sensation before observing it
rituals.target_pattern: Explaining body sensation before observing it
rituals.precise_subpattern: Explaining body sensation before observing it
rituals.vibeLine: Your chest sensation does not need a 14-chapter origin story yet.
rituals.hook: Give the body fifteen seconds before the autobiography begins.
rituals.predict: Guess which explanation your mind will try to add first.
rituals.play: For fifteen seconds, describe only location, size, temperature, movement, pressure and rhythm of the feeling. Every “because” gets deleted.
rituals.catch: Catch how urgently the brain tries to convert sensation into a story about your life.
rituals.reveal: Observation and explanation are separate mental acts, even when they arrive almost together.
rituals.mindBend: Your body can have a sensation without immediately publishing a biography about it.

rituals.name: SIXTY-SECOND PERMISSION
rituals.title: SIXTY-SECOND PERMISSION
rituals.targetPattern: Struggle with emotion amplifying distress
rituals.target_pattern: Struggle with emotion amplifying distress
rituals.precise_subpattern: Struggle with emotion amplifying distress
rituals.vibeLine: Feeling can stay for sixty seconds. We are cancelling the eviction drama.
rituals.hook: For one minute, the feeling is allowed to stay without being fixed.
rituals.predict: Guess what will happen if you stop trying to reduce it for sixty seconds.
rituals.play: Set 60 sec. Say: “You can be here until the timer ends.” Don’t feed the story, soothe, push away or measure every second. Just let the feeling occupy whatever space it already occupies.
rituals.catch: At the bell, notice what changed: intensity, location, texture, or only your struggle with it.
rituals.reveal: Permission does not guarantee the feeling shrinks. It tests whether fighting it was adding a second layer.
rituals.mindBend: You can dislike a feeling without turning its existence into an emergency.

rituals.vibeLine: Turns out “bad” had three ingredients.

rituals.catch: Check if the dominant feeling changes when the smaller colours are allowed in.
rituals.reveal: Mixed emotions are common, but single labels can hide their structure.
rituals.mindBend: You can be 50% angry, 30% hurt and 20% relieved without being inconsistent.

rituals.target_pattern: Emotion treated as a whole-body identity

rituals.vibeLine: Apparently “everywhere” had a surprisingly specific address.
rituals.hook: The feeling says “everywhere.”
rituals.predict: Guess the strongest body location before scanning.
rituals.play: Without changing anything, locate the sensation as precisely as possible: chest centre, left jaw, throat front, stomach upper, forehead, hands. Give it borders if you can.
rituals.catch: Check if the feeling becomes a place in the body rather than the definition of the whole body.
rituals.reveal: Location creates psychological distance without denying intensity.
rituals.mindBend: A sensation can occupy a region without occupying all of you.

Without changing anything, locate the sensation as precisely as possible: chest centre, left jaw, throat front, stomach upper, forehead, hands. Give it borders if you can.

rituals.name: NEED / COMMAND SPLIT
rituals.title: NEED / COMMAND SPLIT
rituals.targetPattern: A legitimate need turning into a rigid demand
rituals.target_pattern: A legitimate need turning into a rigid demand
rituals.precise_subpattern: A legitimate need turning into a rigid demand
rituals.vibeLine: Turns out “I need respect” is different from “you must do exactly this.”
rituals.hook: There may be a real need hiding inside a bossy command.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the sentence softens when “I need them to…” becomes “I need more ___.”
rituals.play: Take the demand involving another person. Translate it into the underlying need without naming what they must do: clarity, rest, respect, space, reassurance, help, fairness, connection.
rituals.catch: Notice how the need remains real while control over the other person loosens.
rituals.reveal: Needs describe what matters to you. Commands prescribe who must satisfy it and how.
rituals.mindBend: A need can be valid without making another person its only delivery system.

rituals.vibeLine: Your body issued breaking news with no new article.
rituals.hook: Your body sent an alarm.
rituals.predict: Guess what fact you know now that you did not know before the anxiety spike.
rituals.play: List any genuinely new external information that arrived with the feeling. If none arrived, write: “New sensation; no new fact.”

rituals.vibeLine: Embarrassed is a state. “Embarrassing human” was an unnecessary job title.

rituals.title: WHAT DOES IT WANT PROTECTED?
rituals.targetPattern: Feeling named without identifying what it protects
rituals.target_pattern: Feeling named without identifying what it protects
rituals.precise_subpattern: Feeling named without identifying what it protects
rituals.vibeLine: Useful alarm, questionable management skills.
rituals.hook: Your emotion may be guarding something specific.
rituals.predict: Guess what matters underneath the feeling: safety, respect, belonging, fairness, rest, competence, autonomy.
rituals.play: Name the emotion. Finish: “If this feeling could protect one thing, it would protect ___.” Don’t turn it into a command for someone else.
rituals.catch: Check if the feeling becomes information about a value or need.
rituals.reveal: Emotions often organise attention around what seems threatened or important.
rituals.mindBend: A feeling can be a guard dog without being the judge.

VIBE: JOLLY

Plot temporarily suspended; feeling still present.

HOOK
For ten seconds, the feeling loses its backstory.

PREDICT
Guess whether the emotion changes when you describe only sensation and urge.

PLAY
Describe the feeling without mentioning who, why, what happened or what it means. Use only body sensation, intensity and action urge.

CATCH
Notice what remains when the plot is removed.

REVEAL
Emotion and narrative are tightly linked but not identical.

MIND BEND
You can feel the feeling without replaying the entire case file.

MOVE ON
↻ PLOTLESS FEELING

rituals.name: EMOTION TRAJECTORY
rituals.title: EMOTION TRAJECTORY
rituals.targetPattern: Current rising emotion assumed to keep rising indefinitely
rituals.target_pattern: Current rising emotion assumed to keep rising indefinitely
rituals.precise_subpattern: Current rising emotion assumed to keep rising indefinitely
rituals.vibeLine: Your emotion graph may not be a rocket launch.
rituals.hook: Your feeling is climbing.
rituals.predict: Guess whether it will rise, plateau or fall over the next few minutes.
rituals.play: Without forcing change, mark the current intensity. Check again after a short ordinary interval. Record direction only: up, flat, down.
rituals.catch: Compare the real direction with the infinite-rise prediction.
rituals.reveal: Emotional systems fluctuate rather than increasing forever.
rituals.mindBend: A rising feeling is a direction, not a promise of endless altitude.

rituals.title: MOVE WITHOUT MOVING IT
rituals.targetPattern: A feeling represented as fixed in one bodily place
rituals.target_pattern: A feeling represented as fixed in one bodily place
rituals.precise_subpattern: A feeling represented as fixed in one bodily place
rituals.vibeLine: Apparently the sensation is not nailed to the floor.
rituals.hook: Do not make the sensation move.
rituals.predict: Guess whether its centre is exactly where it was one minute ago.
rituals.play: Mark the strongest point mentally. After several ordinary breaths or seconds, locate the strongest point again without trying to shift it.
rituals.catch: Notice any change in centre, edge, size or texture.
rituals.reveal: Body sensations are processes, not pinned objects.
rituals.mindBend: A feeling can change address without asking permission.
rituals.ritualCard:
Do not make the sensation move.
Mark the strongest point mentally. After several ordinary breaths or seconds, locate the strongest point again without trying to shift it.
Guess whether its centre is exactly where it was one minute ago.

rituals.name: THREE JOB INTERVIEW
rituals.title: THREE JOB INTERVIEW
rituals.targetPattern: Feeling interpreted as proof of one specific need
rituals.target_pattern: Feeling interpreted as proof of one specific need
rituals.precise_subpattern: Feeling interpreted as proof of one specific need
rituals.vibeLine: Same feeling, multiple possible departments.
rituals.hook: One emotion can apply for more than one job.
rituals.predict: Guess three different things the same feeling might be signalling.
rituals.play: Take anger, sadness, anxiety or guilt. Generate three possible jobs it may be doing here—protecting a boundary, signalling overload, seeking connection, reacting to uncertainty, etc.
rituals.catch: Check if the first explanation loses monopoly status.
rituals.reveal: Emotions are informative but not one-to-one diagnostic codes.
rituals.mindBend: A feeling can be accurate about importance without being precise about cause.

rituals.vibeLine: Loud does not come with a lifetime warranty.
rituals.hook: The feeling is loud.
rituals.predict: Guess how intense it will be in fifteen minutes if nothing dramatic changes.

rituals.reveal: Intensity and duration are different properties of emotion.
rituals.mindBend: A loud feeling is not a stopwatch.

rituals.target_pattern: Body prepared for action that situation does not require

rituals.vibeLine: Ready to run? Great. Is there actually anywhere to run from?

rituals.predict: Guess the action your body seems prepared to perform: run, fight, freeze, hide, speak, hold, check.

rituals.catch: Catch the difference between preparation and necessity.
rituals.reveal: Emotions organise the body for action before conscious decision.
rituals.mindBend: Prepared is not the same as required.

rituals.vibeLine: Maybe the meeting is annoying. Maybe you also skipped lunch.
rituals.hook: This feeling may have arrived from somewhere else and attached itself to the nearest story.
rituals.predict: Guess what non-story factor could be contributing: sleep, hunger, caffeine, noise, heat, illness, deadline, social overload.
rituals.play: List three current body or environment factors before interpreting the emotion. Don’t decide which is responsible—just put them on the board.
rituals.catch: Check if the emotional story becomes less monopolistic.
rituals.reveal: Arousal can be real while its source remains ambiguous.
rituals.mindBend: Feelings need a source check before they become explanations.

rituals.name: CHANCE VS COST
rituals.title: CHANCE VS COST
rituals.targetPattern: Probability and consequence fused into one threat feeling
rituals.target_pattern: Probability and consequence fused into one threat feeling
rituals.precise_subpattern: Probability and consequence fused into one threat feeling
rituals.vibeLine: Awful does not automatically mean probable.
rituals.hook: Fear often multiplies two questions into one feeling.
rituals.predict: Guess which is driving more of the reaction: 'How likely?' or 'How bad if it happens?'
rituals.play: Rate probability 0–10 and consequence 0–10 separately. Ask which number has actual evidence behind it.
rituals.catch: Check if one high number had been dragging the other upward.
rituals.reveal: Threat appraisal combines likelihood and consequence, but they are not the same variable.
rituals.mindBend: Terrible and likely are different words for a reason.

rituals.name: BORED OR FULL?
rituals.title: BORED OR FULL?
rituals.targetPattern: Under-stimulation confused with overload or depletion
rituals.target_pattern: Under-stimulation confused with overload or depletion
rituals.precise_subpattern: Under-stimulation confused with overload or depletion
rituals.vibeLine: Maybe you do not need entertainment. Maybe you need fewer tabs.
rituals.hook: Boredom can mean 'not enough' or 'I have no capacity left.'
rituals.predict: Guess which one fits better right now: under-stimulated, over-stimulated, tired, trapped, or uninterested.
rituals.play: Imagine adding more stimulation—music, scrolling, conversation. Imagine removing stimulation. Which image feels more relieving?
rituals.catch: Check if boredom is asking for more input or less.
rituals.reveal: Similar labels can hide opposite regulatory needs.
rituals.mindBend: Bored is not always hungry for entertainment.

VIBE: CHEEKY

Maybe you do not need entertainment. Maybe you need fewer tabs.

HOOK
Boredom can mean 'not enough' or 'I have no capacity left.'

PREDICT
Guess which one fits better right now: under-stimulated, over-stimulated, tired, trapped, or uninterested.

PLAY
Imagine adding more stimulation—music, scrolling, conversation. Imagine removing stimulation. Which image feels more relieving?

CATCH
Check if boredom is asking for more input or less.

REVEAL
Similar labels can hide opposite regulatory needs.

MIND BEND
Bored is not always hungry for entertainment.

MOVE ON
↻ BORED OR FULL?

rituals.vibeLine: A room full of humans is not automatically company.

rituals.reveal: Loneliness responds to perceived connection, not simply headcount.
rituals.mindBend: A crowded room can be socially empty.

rituals.title: CHANGE IT OR CARRY IT?
rituals.targetPattern: Same emotion requiring different response depending on whether the situation can change
rituals.target_pattern: Same emotion requiring different response depending on whether the situation can change
rituals.precise_subpattern: Same emotion requiring different response depending on whether the situation can change
rituals.vibeLine: Fix the leak; stop negotiating with rain.
rituals.hook: Before regulating the feeling, check whether the situation itself is movable.
rituals.predict: Guess: is the main problem controllable now, partly controllable, or not controllable today?
rituals.play: Put the issue in one box. CONTROLLABLE: choose 1 action. PARTLY: choose your piece. NOT NOW: choose one way to carry the feeling safely.
rituals.catch: Notice how the regulation strategy changes with controllability.
rituals.reveal: Coping works better when strategy matches what can actually be changed.
rituals.mindBend: Do not use acceptance on a fixable leak—or a wrench on the weather.

rituals.name: RELIEF ADDS EXTRA STARS
rituals.title: RELIEF ADDS EXTRA STARS
rituals.targetPattern: Relief after uncertainty making the safe outcome feel exceptionally good
rituals.target_pattern: Relief after uncertainty making the safe outcome feel exceptionally good
rituals.precise_subpattern: Relief after uncertainty making the safe outcome feel exceptionally good
rituals.vibeLine: Thank-god lighting is extremely flattering.
rituals.hook: Relief can make ordinary safety feel euphoric for a minute.
rituals.predict: Guess how you would rate the outcome if you had never feared the bad alternative first.
rituals.play: Take a recent 'thank god' moment. Imagine the same neutral-good outcome arriving without the preceding scare.
rituals.catch: Notice how much of the glow belongs to the outcome versus the contrast.
rituals.reveal: Relief is partly a contrast response to expected threat ending.
rituals.mindBend: The outcome may be good; relief adds bonus lighting.

rituals.name: DISAPPOINTMENT HAS TWO NUMBERS
rituals.title: DISAPPOINTMENT HAS TWO NUMBERS
rituals.targetPattern: Disappointment intensity driven by forecast rather than absolute outcome
rituals.target_pattern: Disappointment intensity driven by forecast rather than absolute outcome
rituals.precise_subpattern: Disappointment intensity driven by forecast rather than absolute outcome
rituals.vibeLine: Seven feels awful when you preordered ten.
rituals.hook: Disappointment is not only what happened.
rituals.predict: Guess the size of the gap between expected and actual outcome.
rituals.play: Rate EXPECTED outcome 0–10 and ACTUAL outcome 0–10. Look at the gap separately from the actual result.

rituals.vibeLine: Same heartbeat, different road sign.

rituals.predict: Guess which label changes what you want to do: 'I'm anxious' versus 'my body is getting ready.'

rituals.catch: Notice how the same arousal can support more than one appraisal.
rituals.reveal: Physiological activation is not emotionally self-explanatory.
rituals.mindBend: The engine can rev before the road tells you why.

rituals.name: TRY 5% OPPOSITE
rituals.title: TRY 5% OPPOSITE
rituals.targetPattern: Action urge maintaining emotion when situation no longer fits it
rituals.target_pattern: Action urge maintaining emotion when situation no longer fits it
rituals.precise_subpattern: Action urge maintaining emotion when situation no longer fits it
rituals.vibeLine: No personality makeover. Just one degree on the steering wheel.
rituals.hook: Your emotion is leaning one direction.
rituals.predict: Guess the action urge: withdraw, avoid eye contact, hunch, rush, over-explain, freeze.
rituals.play: If safe and the urge does not fit the facts, do only 5% opposite: shoulders slightly open, one extra sentence, one slower step, stay 30 sec longer.
rituals.catch: Check if emotion, body, or prediction changes.
rituals.reveal: Behaviour can feed emotional states as well as express them.
rituals.mindBend: You do not need a dramatic opposite action; a five-percent experiment can teach you.

rituals.mindBend: The second event may not have created all the intensity it received.

rituals.targetPattern: Worry maintaining a steady negative state partly to avoid the emotional jolt of bad surprise

rituals.precise_subpattern: Worry maintaining a steady negative state partly to avoid the emotional jolt of bad surprise
rituals.vibeLine: Premium: all-day tension.
rituals.hook: Staying tense can feel safer than relaxing and being shocked later.
rituals.predict: Guess whether calm feels risky because bad news would then hit harder.
rituals.play: Imagine two paths: stay worried all day then hear bad news, or have one calm hour then hear the same bad news. Notice which transition you fear more.
rituals.catch: Catch the preference for steady discomfort over emotional contrast.
rituals.reveal: Some worry is maintained by avoidance of sudden negative emotional shifts.
rituals.mindBend: Constant tension can function like emotional shock insurance.

rituals.vibeLine: Threat math was missing half the spreadsheet.

rituals.reveal: Stress responses differ when demands are appraised as exceeding versus being met by coping resources.
rituals.mindBend: The task can stay hard while the internal equation changes.

rituals.target_pattern: Ordinary stress activation being interpreted only as evidence of malfunction
rituals.precise_subpattern: Ordinary stress activation being interpreted only as evidence of malfunction
rituals.vibeLine: Uncomfortable does not automatically mean malfunctioning.
rituals.hook: A racing system can be read as 'I'm failing' or 'my body is mobilising.'
rituals.predict: Guess which interpretation you automatically attach to ordinary stress activation.
rituals.play: Take one safe stress cue—alertness, faster heart, energy. Write DEBILITATING STORY and MOBILISING STORY without pretending the sensation is pleasant.
rituals.catch: Notice which story changes what you do next.
rituals.reveal: Stress mindsets influence appraisal and behavioural responses to stress.
rituals.mindBend: The sensation can be uncomfortable without meaning the system is useless.

rituals.precise_subpattern: Incidental anger increasing certainty in an unrelated ambiguous judgment
rituals.vibeLine: No new facts, much louder verdict.
rituals.hook: Anger can make unrelated judgments feel more certain than the evidence became.
rituals.predict: Guess which decision suddenly feels obvious while you are angry.

rituals.catch: Check if certainty moves while facts stay fixed.
rituals.reveal: Anger carries appraisals of certainty and control that can spill into later judgments.
rituals.mindBend: The feeling can lend confidence to a question it did not answer.
